body.statement:
After substituting \(P_1=\mu\), \(P_2=(-\operatorname{Id})_{\#}
u\), and \(P_3=\cdots=P_K=\delta_0\) into the definition of \(L\), one has definitionally \(K^2L(\mathbf P)=\inf_{\pi\in\Gamma(\mu,
u)}\int\|x-y\|_2^2\,d\pi(x,y)=W_2^2(\mu,
u)\).
body.justification: This sanity-reduction helper checks normalization and transfers the published two-margin obstruction; it is not counted as a research contribution.
body.gap: The identity is a direct definitional specialization, so no novelty is claimed for it; the unresolved work is the genuinely all-arm rematching obstruction.
body.consumer: The exact-frontier question must dominate the scaled two-margin modulus and preserve its fixed-\(K\) logarithmic issue.
body.proof_tex:
Under the stated substitution, coordinates \(Z_3,\ldots,Z_K\) equal zero almost surely. If \(Z_1=X\sim\mu\) and \(Z_2=-Y\) with \(Y\sim\nu\), the joint law of \((X,Y)\) is a coupling \(\pi\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu)\), and conversely every such \(\pi\) induces exactly one admissible \(K\)-coupling after adjoining the deterministic zero coordinates. Therefore the definition of \(L\) gives
\[
K^2L(\mathbf P)
=\inf_{\pi\in\Gamma(\mu,\nu)}\int\|x-y\|_2^2\,d\pi(x,y)
=W_2^2(\mu,\nu).
\]
No centering term is introduced: this is an identity for the second-moment endpoint \(L\).
